About the Lodge

141 Years of Brotherhood in West Texas

Staked Plains Lodge No. 598 was chartered on December 12, 1884, under the Grand Lodge of Texas, A.F. & A.M. For more than a century, we have met on the South Main Street in Big Spring — the same community we have served since the Permian Basin was open range.

In 1885, Lodge members helped establish what would become Mount Olive Cemetery, one of the oldest burial grounds in Howard County. That act of civic responsibility is characteristic of who we are: a fraternity that takes seriously its obligation to the place it calls home.

What Is Freemasonry

A Brotherhood Built on Timeless Principles

Freemasonry is believed to be the world's oldest fraternal organization. It brings together men of good character — across every background, profession, and walk of life — in a shared commitment to personal growth, mutual support, and service to community.

Membership is not inherited or sold. It is earned through a man's own desire to improve himself and contribute to something larger than himself. What happens inside our Lodge room belongs to the Brethren. What you will find outside it is men who take that experience seriously.

Brotherly Love

Masons are taught to regard the whole human species as one family, to aid, support, and protect one another.

Relief

To relieve the distressed is a duty incumbent on all men, but particularly on Masons. To soothe the unhappy, to sympathize with their misfortunes, and to restore peace to troubled minds — this is the aim of the Craft.

Truth

Masons are taught to be honest in all dealings — with their Brethren, their families, and the world. Truth is not a concept to Masons; it is a daily practice.

Freemasonry has been practiced in Texas since the Republic. Among its members: Sam Houston, Stephen F. Austin, and Mirabeau B. Lamar. The tradition continues in Big Spring.

Service & Giving

Masonic Charities

Texas Masons support a broad network of charitable programs — many operated statewide, all funded without public solicitation.

  • Masonic Children & Family Services of Texas
  • Texas Scottish Rite Hospital for Children
  • Shriner's Hospitals for Children
  • Texas Masonic Retirement Community
  • DeMolay International
  • Rainbow Girls & Job's Daughters
Staked Plains Lodge in the Community
Fantastic Teeth Fan Club

Each year, Lodge members deliver free dental hygiene kits to first graders at Big Spring elementary schools — part of a statewide program that has reached over 1.4 million Texas children.

Mirabeau B. Lamar Award of Excellence

Annual recognition for outstanding Big Spring educators, presented at the Howard County school district's awards ceremony. Named for Mirabeau B. Lamar — Mason, President of the Republic of Texas, and Father of Texas Education.

Teachers Appreciation Dinner

Lodge members host and cook an annual dinner for Big Spring educators at the lodge hall — a personal expression of the fraternity's historic commitment to public education.

Annual Senior Scholarships

Scholarships awarded to graduating Big Spring seniors through an essay competition. Candidates' essays are read in open Lodge; recipients are selected by vote of the Brethren.

Becoming a Mason

How to Join

Freemasonry does not recruit. A man petitions of his own free will, and his petition is considered by the Brethren on the merits of his character. If you are a man of good standing who wants to know more, reach out. That is the first step.

Who is eligible to petition?
Any man of good moral character, at least 18 years of age, who believes in a Supreme Being and comes to Freemasonry of his own free will. No man is solicited or pressured to join.
What does membership involve?
Membership involves regular attendance at Lodge meetings, participation in the degrees of Masonry, a commitment to the principles of the fraternity, and payment of annual dues. The time investment is real and meaningful.
What are the degrees of Masonry?
Texas Freemasonry confers three degrees: Entered Apprentice, Fellow Craft, and Master Mason. Each degree is a distinct experience. The content of the degrees is not published — it is meant to be lived, not read about in advance.
How long does the process take?
The timeline varies by Lodge and candidate. From petition to Master Mason typically takes several months. The Lodge moves at a pace that serves the candidate and the Brethren.
Do I need to know a Mason to join?
You do not. Contact us directly. We will answer your questions honestly and, if you are interested, guide you through the petition process.
